purpose: Define the public-safe SEIS DevOps/SRE observability and incident contract so CI, release, cloud, SSH, AI routing, rollback, restore-drill, and audit evidence can be tracked without claiming live telemetry or production authority.
truthBoundary: This contract is a readiness and evidence model. It is not live monitoring, production telemetry, incident automation, cloud mutation authority, SSH execution authority, and not proof that any external provider dashboard is connected.

readinessLevels.meaning: Evidence comes from local files and deterministic checks only.
A command or release path can be simulated without changing external systems.
The change is reviewable and has focused local evidence.
Local gates and PR review evidence are ready for release decision.
Production-like work is blocked behind explicit owner approval, credentials outside the public repo, and rollback proof.
A suspected quality, security, release, provider, or cloud issue is being tracked with redacted evidence.
Recovery behavior is tested or rehearsed without destructive external action.
Infrastructure-as-code intent is reviewed as a plan only.
Infrastructure mutation remains blocked until explicit owner approval, dry-run evidence, rollback, and secret isolation are present.

sliSloCatalog.sli: Targeted checker pass rate for the selected PR slice.
sliSloCatalog.slo: Every merged PR-ready slice has its direct checker and adjacent governance checks reported.
sliSloCatalog.measurementSource: npm scripts and clean snapshot validation

sliSloCatalog.slo: No public release is claimed while public readiness blockers are open.

sliSloCatalog.sli: Provider route state distinguishes installed, visible, credentialed, quotaReady, verified, rate-limited, and blocked.
sliSloCatalog.slo: No live AI route is claimed without current-run readiness evidence.
sliSloCatalog.measurementSource: provider registry and future routing ledger

sliSloCatalog.sli: SSH/cloud actions remain credential-free and approval-gated.
sliSloCatalog.slo: No SSH execution or cloud mutation occurs without explicit approval, dry-run, and rollback note.
sliSloCatalog.measurementSource: SEIS-SSH access model and deployment docs

alertSeverities.label: Critical security or destructive external mutation risk
alertSeverities.response: Stop, preserve evidence, do not print secrets, request owner approval for any mutation.

alertSeverities.label: Release-blocking quality, CI, or public-readiness failure
alertSeverities.response: Block release claim, record failing command, define rollback or fix-forward path.

alertSeverities.label: Degraded route, provider limit, missing external evidence, or partial verification
alertSeverities.response: Mark route blocked or rate-limited, use deterministic validator or lower-risk fallback.

alertSeverities.label: Documentation, handoff, or observability gap
alertSeverities.response: Track in backlog, attach checker when practical, keep status honest.

completionDefinition: Readiness levels cover local-only, dry-run, pr-ready, release-candidate, production-gated, incident, restore-drill, iac-plan, and iac-apply.
SLI/SLO records identify measurement source and current status without claiming live monitoring.
Incident severities and states define response behavior without printing secrets or mutating external systems.
Audit log fields include approval, rollback, redaction, and external mutation markers.
The runbook, docs index, checker script, and full-usage backlog all point to this contract.
nextSafeActions: Add a release promotion matrix that consumes these readiness levels.
Add a redacted LLM routing decision ledger for AI provider incident and rate-limit state.
Add a future dashboard view only after the static contract and checker remain stable.
